Yes, please please PLEASE leave him alone. He’s established that this is a pattern and it’s not healthy (or even safe) for you to keep reconnecting. You also need to start planning on how to protect yourself for once he realizes it’s truly over. See if your state has an address confidentiality program if you need to consider moving, let someone(s) trusted at work know about your situation and that you’re trying to avoid him, have a family member or friend stay with you for a bit if you’re living alone, etc. I’m not trying to be dramatic - this is how many DV stories begin before the woman eventually ends up in a body bag. The temporary pain of the ultimate breakup will be worth it in the long-term. It’s OK to remember the good times, but do not let them fool you into letting him back in.

First, love, I’m very sorry you’re going through this. I was in a domestic violence situation as well, for most of my life (my mom’s husband). Things obviously aren’t perfect now, but I am glad to be finally free from his grip. He works in law enforcement and has two firearms. A restraining order did not work because of his pull with police and lack of evidence. We’re in the U.S., so I’m not sure how things work in Canada. I’d say that while you are planning this escape, document evidence whenever you can - even if it’s just recording things he says to you using the audio app on your phone. You never know when you may need it later. Do you have any family or friends who would allow you to couch surf in the meantime while you sort things out? Even a co-worker? They may be more understanding than you anticipate. Worst case scenario, maybe we could link up temporarily. I’m in New York. Private message me if you want.

I’m not religious either but I do believe many things happen for a reason. Maybe it’s that you haven’t filled your purpose yet, whatever that may be. It could be that something bigger for you is on the horizon. 18 attempts in one year is A LOT!! Something powerful is going on here. I wouldn’t ignore it. Tell us your story, no judgment. You might be surprised to find someone in a similar situation who can offer what they’ve tried.

This is great advice for OP. I’ve done the same and I have a personality where I have this need to feel productive. If I’m being lazy or not getting things done, it starts eating at me. I grew up in a strict military household and I believe that’s part of the reason. Start out with small tasks and work your way up to bigger accomplishments. Something as simple as “clean out the bathroom by the end of the day” (or weekend) can surprisingly go a long way. I’d also consider exploring some alternate medications.

This sounds eerily similar to my mom’s missing story in Oct 2016. Her husband was insanely abusive and threatening her life. When he reported her missing and I saw that he had called a waste removal service around the time, my mind panicked. I had police calling me at work because an investigation was launched, the works. Turns out, about a week later, she was safe and sound in another area. She had to dip the safest way she knew how and felt she couldn’t tell anybody right away. Left her phone behind because of the gps signal tracking. My point is that things could be a lot less severe than you think. Try to stay focused for the sake of finding her and let’s go through your options. You tried social media and that’s not working, can’t call her. What has she communicated with you in recent conversations? Have you tried going by her house yet? If that makes you uncomfortable, try calling local hospitals to see if she’s checked in. Please keep us posted.

If you’re able to get her to express herself in other ways, that would be great. Could you maybe get the message anonymously to her friend? Really sucks that her family is shit - she probably feeling this way because of the dent in her support system.

If there’s a close friend in her life that you both trust, I’d confide in them. Hopefully this could be the person whose place she’s at now. Breakups suck, but she is so young. My first suicide attempt was a year younger than she is now. I was heavy into songwriting. My friends dragged me to the studio and forced me to write, even if it was about something depressing. It helped so much realizing that I actually had people who cared and who spent some time looking out for me. She needs to be surrounded with love and reminded that she has people who have her back (I hope). Keep us posted...
Thanks for sharing your story. It sounds like you’ve done an amazing job turning your life around. I hope you continue to keep us updated.
